tasks.title: Traffic on the River Seine
tasks.statement: As you journey along the river, there are many boats moored at the riverside or travelling along the river. On the map on the next page, you can see all the boats that were on the river on Wednesday 5th July at 1400h CEST. Each boat is marked by a coloured dot or an arrow. An arrow means the vessel is moving.

parts.question: How many boats can you see on the river?
parts.reference: 32. (0.5 for both 1A and 1B right)

parts.question: How many boats are moving?
parts.reference: 11. (0.5 for both 1A and 1B right)

parts.question: Four boats are labelled with their names. The four images on this page show the four boats. Use the key to identify each boat and complete the table in your answer book (A - Van Dam, B - Eco Universe, C - Avalon, D - Nirvana).
parts.reference: A: Van Dam, B: Eco Universe, C: Avalon, D: Nirvana. 0.5 if all correct (clue is cranes on the bulk carrier).

parts.question: Use the scale on the map. If the ‘Van Dam’ is travelling at 10 nautical miles per hour, how long will it take for it to travel the length of the River Seine shown on the map?
parts.reference: 5 hours 12 minutes (52 NM). Give 0.5 if they have worked out the correct time for their distance, but the distance is more than 10% out.

tasks.title: Vernier Marsh Vegetation
tasks.statement: We will leave the boat at Cadebec-en-Caux and cross the river. The image shows a view across the Vernier Marsh. This is an area of wetland on the south bank of the River Seine, south of Caudebec-en-Caux on the map.

parts.question: How do wetlands form? Read the causes of formation listed below and write T (true) or F (false) in the boxes on the answer sheet (i. Where the water table is at or near the surface, ii. Where buried ice from glaciers has melted, iii. Where beavers have made dams to stop streamflow, iv. Where rivers constantly overflow their banks).
parts.reference: i: T, ii: T, iii: T, iv: T. 0.5 if all correct.

parts.question: Look at the two images and give TWO management issues for farmers on this area of land.
parts.reference: flooded land/communication/stagnant water/any other reasonable option. 0.5 marks.

parts.question: Give one reason why willow trees have been planted along a drainage channel.
parts.reference: willow thrives in wet environments and will help with drainage. 0.5 marks for full explanation.

parts.question: Besides providing meat and dairy products, why else might the farmers keep cattle on their land?
parts.reference: cows will graze and keep the vegetation from overgrowing / this type of cattle is very attractive and can be tourist attractions. 0.5 marks for full explanation.

parts.question: Estimate the percentage of vegetation cover and bare ground inside this quadrat.
parts.reference: 55% vegetation 45% bare ground (+/- 10%) must be more vegetation than bare ground. 1 mark.

parts.question: The quadrat measure 0.5m x 0.5m What is the actual area that the bare ground covers?
parts.reference: 0.138 metres squared. 0.5 marks.

parts.question: The three boxes show different types of sampling methods. On your answer sheet, give names for each of the different types of sampling (A, B, C).
parts.reference: A: random, B: systematic, C: stratified. 0.5 marks for 2/3 right.

tasks.title: Vernier Marsh Soils
tasks.statement: This map shows the geology of the area of the Vernier Marsh. Three soil pits were dug at locations A, B and C. Look at the next page and decide which soil was found at each site.

parts.question: Write the number of the correct profile in the right box for locations A, B, and C.
parts.reference: A: 1, B: 2, C: 3. 1 mark for all correct (0.5 marks for 1 correct).

parts.question: Give TWO factors that influence the formation of soils besides geology/bedrock.
parts.reference: 2 from climate/time/relief/organisms. 1 mark.

parts.question: Look at the key showing the different types of bedrock in the area. (i) Which material was not deposited in water? (ii) Which are the youngest deposits in the area?
parts.reference: (i) loess. (ii) Holocene alluvial deposits. 1 mark.

tasks.title: The River Channel
tasks.statement: The Vernier Marsh lies inside the course of an old meander. The Seine Estuary can be divided into three zones that can be distinguished from upstream to downstream: 1. The fluvial estuary between Poses and Vieux-Port... 2. The middle estuary or brackish estuary... 3. The marine estuary between Honfleur and the eastern part of the Seine Bay...

parts.question: Use the map on the response sheet to sketch the probable former course of the River Seine in prehistoric times. Mark the channel clearly.
parts.reference: 1 mark – must join the current channel at both ends otherwise 0.5 marks for correct channel.

parts.question: Mark the three zones onto the base map of the River Seine in your response sheet. Label each one clearly with the name and salinity of the zone.
parts.reference: 1 mark for 2 accurate lines.

parts.question: Identify a place in the estuary where this photo could have been taken. Mark the position on the map with a large Star *.
parts.reference: 1 mark for star – must be on the river in central zone (nearer the sea).

tasks.title: Volume of cargo at Le Havre Port
tasks.statement: The Port of Le Havre is the 6th busiest port in Europe. The table shows the number of containers passing through the port between 2011 and 2018. After leaving the boat at Berville-sur-mer, you board a coach to travel west. You cross the Normandie Bridge to return to Paris. It is the lowest crossing point of the River Seine.

parts.question: Complete the graph on your response sheet to show the information in the table.
parts.reference: Should be a line graph / Year on x axis, units on y axis / Points accurately drawn / Joined together with straight lines (1 mark for axes, 1 mark for line/bars).

parts.question: What is the percentage increase in the number of containers between 2011 and 2018?
In which compass direction will you be travelling across the bridge?
parts.reference: North. 0.5 marks.
